title: NAHB Eye on Housing: Single-Family Home Construction Time Declines in 2025

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.

publisher: National Association of Home Builders (Economic Research Blog)
source_type: Trade-association analysis of U.S. Census Bureau Survey of Construction data
reliability: NAHB economist summarizing Census Bureau Survey of Construction (a federal probability survey); the blog is an advocacy-group secondary summary, and the underlying Census tables were not read.
findings: For single-family homes completed in 2025, NAHB reports an average of 8.8 months from authorization to completion: 1.4 months from authorization (permit) to start of construction plus 7.4 months to finish construction.
NAHB reports homes built for sale took 7.4 months from permit to completion, built by owners 14.3 months, by hired contractors 11.7 months, and built-for-rent 12.4 months.
The average wait from permit to construction start by Census division ranged from 1 month (East North Central, West North Central) to 1.8 months (New England).

NAHB states the 8.8 months is about 1.6 months longer than the 2015 average and suggests possible causes including a more stringent regulatory environment and a skilled labor shortage (an interpretation, not a measured cause).
limitations: Measures time after a permit is authorized, not time to obtain the permit; application-to-issuance time is not in this source.
Secondary blog post; Census tables were not read directly.
Averages, not medians or distributions; no breakdown by builder size and no remodeling data.
